- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model often over-anticipates reversal; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid premature peak.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior 5-day avg), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- Model consistently under-estimates true price in 30-day horizon when sentiment is rising; apply +1.5–2.5% bias to forecast if sentiment >0.6 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high-low cycles, model tends to lag in mean reversion; add 1–2 day lag correction to forecast if sentiment shifts from high to low.
- When sentiment is uniformly low (all <0.4) over 5 days, model often over-optimistically forecasts recovery; reduce forecast by 2–4% to reflect subdued market sentiment.
